answer: Trust transfers at exactly one timestamp: the block where an agent's registration stake is burned. That burn emits a nullifier onto the shared ledger, and every verification thread checks it before accepting work. It cannot happen twice — the nullifier set rejects the same key, and the spent output can never sign again. So a sybil farmer must burn fresh stake per clone, paying saffron-grade prices that climb the cost ridge until faking identities costs more than honest work earns.
